definition: An equation giving the rate of a reaction as the rate constant multiplied by each reactant concentration (and sometimes a catalyst's) raised to its order, such as $\text{rate} = k[\text{A}]^{m}[\text{B}]^{n}$; it can only be found by experiment.
The power to which a reactant's concentration is raised in the rate equation; the overall order is the sum of the orders for all the reactants.
The constant $k$ in a rate equation: it changes with temperature but not with concentration, and its units depend on the overall order of the reaction.
